newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end mixed in listless trade.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end mixed in listless trade.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed after a day of what brokers described as listless and mostly directionless trade in Bogota and Medellin.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index edged up 0.06 percent to 13,263.61 in volume of 938.40 pesos, while Bogota's IBB closed down 0.28 percent at 840.27 on lower-than-average volume of just 232.7 million pesos.
"The markets were dead today,"one disgruntled broker said.
Barring major news on the economic or political front, he said trading could remain in the doldrums for the rest of the year.
Flagging economic growth, political uncertainty and concerns about ties with the United States, have all put a damper on stocks, the broker said.

Losers in Bogota included heavily traded brewer Bavaria SA, which fell 1.07 percent to end at 3,957 pesos per share, and cement maker Cementos Argos, which dropped 1.30 percent to end at 5,280 pesos per share.
Carulla SA, Colombia's leading supermarket chain, also closed sharply lower, dropping 1.70 percent to end the day at 5,700 pesos a share.
"Small investors followed the advice of their brokers and were selling to transfer their funds into fixed income," one broker said in explaining the day's losses in Bogota.

In Medellin, brokers said foreign fund buying helped drive Cementos Argos up 1.06 percent to close at 5,255 pesos per share. Bavaria tracked its losses in Bogota, however, dropping 0.50 percent to end at 3,980. Retail chain Cadenalco, another decliner, fell 1.12 percent to end at 880 pesos per share.
Thinly-traded steelmaker Siderurgica de Medellin, the day's big winner, jumped 14.2 percent to close at 240 as traders jockeyed for position ahead of its upcoming sale.
